transcript.answer: It falls back to the most restrictive authority, `requires_human_action`. The lookup function `authorityOf(table, name)` in `apps/api/src/oversight/toolAuthority.ts` returns `table[name]` only if the table has its own entry for that name (checked with `Object.hasOwn`). Otherwise it returns `'requires_human_action'`. The result is that an unknown tool is never treated as read-only or auto-permitted. It needs a human to act. Using `Object.hasOwn` also means inherited property names such as `toString` or `constructor` can't match a row by accident. I read this from the code snippet only. I did not look at the callers, so I can't say exactly how `requires_human_action` is enforced downstream.
